messages:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing an outbound-only tunnel agent for Private deployments instead of VPC peering/PrivateLink. Short summary: customers run a lightweight agent in their VPC that establishes an mTLS reverse tunnel to a regional control/proxy fleet we manage. Benefits: no cross-account peering, fits strict network policies, easier for air-gapped-ish setups. Downsides: agent lifecycle + egress cost, connection scaling, and potential latency. Thoughts?

olivia: +1 for exploring. two quick q's: how do we handle long-lived streaming (websockets)? NAT timeouts will kill streams. :thinking:

sam: Good call. agent will support TCP multiplexing + application-level keepalives. plan is WebSocket (or HTTP/2) over a persistent upstream with periodic pings (30s) and reconnect/backoff. also support multi-conn mode for high throughput.

daniel: TLS/termination question — do we terminate TLS at our proxy or keep end-to-end? we should avoid decrypting customer traffic by default for compliance.

sam: We keep customer TLS end-to-end for data plane traffic. Control plane and agent management use mTLS to our CA. If a customer explicitly opts into payload inspection (rare), we can TLS-terminate with explicit consent and controls.

tayla: What about cert provisioning/rotation for agents? we can't have customers doing manual certs.

sam: Short-lived certs issued by our CA during bootstrap. Agent takes a bootstrap token (customer-provided) to GET a signed cert. rotation is automated (default TTL 7d), with local cache if CA unreachable. fallback: token refresh flow via Console. Example agent config:
```yaml
agent:
  region: us-west-2
  bootstrap_token: REPLACE_ME
  connections: 2  # fallback multi-conn
  keepalive_sec: 30
```

kevin: Perf question: TCP multiplexing can cause head-of-line blocking for large requests; how do we avoid that?

sam: We'll use HTTP/2 or a multiplexed RPC (like grpc) to reduce HOL; for pathological cases we allow striping across N connections. benchmarking will drive default N.

olivia: Observability — what telemetry does the agent emit? we need per-tenant metrics but not payloads.

sam: Minimal telemetry by default: connection health, bytes in/out, RTT, per-route counters. Traces are opt-in and only if customer consents; logs are metadata-only (no request payload). telemetry goes over mTLS channel.

daniel: Can we design routing so customers can switch from agent->peering/privatelink later without major changes? rolling upgrades need to be simple.

sam: Yes — control plane routing will be endpoint-agnostic. each tenant has an ordered list of endpoint types (peering, privatelink, agent). we can failover or prefer one over another. that'll let us A/B or canary with minimal config changes.

kevin: Any implications for cost model? egress bandwidth from customer VPCs might be billable and messy. we need to reflect that in pricing or docs.

sam: Agreed — ops and pricing teams need to surface egress delta. also we'll provide a small on-agent cache for common responses to reduce repeated egress.

infra-bot: deploy:agent-proxy-alpha -> us-west-2 succeeded :white_check_mark:

tayla: Thanks - next steps: I'll draft an RFC with perf targets, security checklist (CA flow, token lifecycle), and rollout plan. assign: @sam to build proto agent + load test harness; @olivia to design observability knobs. target: EOW for alpha demo. :rocket:
